summary.en: Express database questions as safe logical conditions using tuple and domain variables.
summary.bn: টিউপল ও ডোমেইন ভেরিয়েবল দিয়ে নিরাপদ যৌক্তিক শর্তে ডেটাবেসের প্রশ্ন প্রকাশ করো।

notes: CHECK constraints are enforced from MySQL 8.0.16. The examples also run on MySQL 8.4.

sections.title: Describe the answer with a condition
Say what qualifies and what must exist

examples.title: An existential condition in SQL
examples.explanationHtml: The witness is a result with at least 80 marks. Students 101, 102 and 104 have such a result, and each student appears once.

examples.title: Every enrollment has a result
examples.explanationHtml: Only student 107 has an enrollment without a result. Student 108 qualifies because there is no enrollment that violates the rule: this is vacuous truth.

practice.title: Write a tuple predicate
practice.statementHtml: Express the IDs of CSE students using tuple relational calculus.
hints: State the variable’s range before its comparison.
practice.answerHtml: {s.student_id | Students(s) ∧ s.department_id = 1}. Students(s) restricts s to existing student tuples. The department condition keeps only CSE rows. The result projects student_id, not the whole tuple.

practice.title: Use a result witness
practice.statementHtml: Express students who have at least one mark of 80 or more.
hints: A high result belonging to a different student is not a witness.
practice.answerHtml: {s.student_id | Students(s) ∧ ∃r (Results(r) ∧ r.student_id = s.student_id ∧ r.marks ≥ 80)}. The witness r must belong to the same student. Ayesha, Tanvir and Rafi qualify in the university data.

practice.title: Translate to domain variables
practice.statementHtml: For S(id, name, dept), express names in department 1 using domain relational calculus.
hints: Bind all fields of the relation, even fields not returned.
practice.answerHtml: {<n> | ∃i ∃d (S(i,n,d) ∧ d = 1)}. Each variable holds one attribute value. The relation predicate binds the three values to the same row. The existential variables do not appear in the returned one-column tuple.

practice.title: Avoid vacuous acceptance
practice.statementHtml: A scholarship rule requires at least one enrollment and a result for every enrollment. Explain both parts.
hints: Try the rule on a student with no enrollment rows.
practice.answerHtml: First require an enrollment witness for the student. Then require that no enrollment lacks a matching result. Without the first part, Fahim, who has no enrollments, satisfies the universal condition vacuously. The scholarship rule deliberately excludes him.

practice.title: Repair an unsafe complement
practice.statementHtml: Explain why {x | NOT Students(x)} is unsafe and describe a finite alternative.
hints: An absence condition needs a defined set of candidates.
practice.answerHtml: The complement can include unlimited tuples outside Students, so the answer depends on an unspecified universe. Start instead from a finite relation such as Applicants(x), then keep applicants absent from Students. Both the range and comparison keys must be explicit.

quiz.prompt: How does calculus differ from an algebra expression?
options: It states a condition answers must satisfy
quiz.explanation: Calculus expresses what qualifies, while algebra composes operations; neither prescribes a physical plan.

quiz.prompt: What does a tuple variable represent in tuple relational calculus?
options: A complete tuple from a relation
quiz.explanation: Tuple variables have named attributes and range over relation rows.

quiz.prompt: What does a domain variable represent?
quiz.explanation: Domain calculus uses variables for individual column values.

quiz.prompt: What does ∃r mean in a database predicate?
quiz.explanation: The existential quantifier asks for at least one witness satisfying the predicate.

quiz.prompt: What does ∀e mean over a stated enrollment range?
options: Every enrollment in that range must meet the condition
quiz.explanation: Universal quantification tests each member of the stated range.

quiz.prompt: Why restrict a calculus variable to Students?
options: To give it a finite database range
quiz.explanation: Range restriction prevents answers from wandering over unrelated values outside the database.

quiz.prompt: What is wrong with asking for all x that are not stored students without a finite range?
options: It may describe infinitely many outside values
It is exactly a primary-key constraint
quiz.explanation: An unrestricted complement can include unlimited values absent from stored relations.

quiz.prompt: Which SQL construct naturally expresses an existential witness?
quiz.explanation: EXISTS checks whether a subquery has at least one qualifying row.

quiz.prompt: A student has no enrollments. Does every enrollment have a result for that student hold?
options: No, because the student must fail
Only if a zero mark is inserted
Only if the name is known
Yes, vacuously, unless a separate existence condition is required
quiz.explanation: There is no counterexample enrollment; requiring at least one enrollment is an additional predicate.

quiz.prompt: How does SQL differ from classical safe calculus?
options: SQL has duplicates and NULL unless handled explicitly
quiz.explanation: DISTINCT and explicit NULL rules may be needed to match classical set-based logic.

quiz.prompt: Which formula states that every required section is enrolled?
options: There is no required section without a matching enrollment
quiz.explanation: Universal conditions can be rewritten as absence of a counterexample.

quiz.prompt: What does domain independence mean here?
options: Every column must use the same SQL type
Answers do not change when unrelated outside values enlarge the universe
quiz.explanation: A safe expression derives its answers from relevant finite data rather than an arbitrary outside domain.

keyPoints.en: Calculus describes qualifying answers through predicates.
keyPoints.bn: ক্যালকুলাসে শর্ত দিয়ে কাঙ্ক্ষিত উত্তর বর্ণনা করা হয়।

keyPoints.en: Tuple variables range over complete relation rows.
keyPoints.bn: টিউপল ভেরিয়েবল একটি রিলেশনের পুরো সারি বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: Domain variables represent individual attribute values.
keyPoints.bn: ডোমেইন ভেরিয়েবল আলাদা অ্যাট্রিবিউটের মান বোঝায়।

keyPoints.en: Existential quantification asks whether a witness exists.
keyPoints.bn: অস্তিত্বসূচক কোয়ান্টিফায়ার খোঁজে অন্তত একটি প্রমাণ আছে কি না।

keyPoints.en: Safe expressions restrict answers to database-derived values.
keyPoints.bn: নিরাপদ এক্সপ্রেশনে উত্তর ডেটাবেস থেকে পাওয়া মানে সীমিত থাকে।

examQuestions.question: Compare tuple and domain calculus with one department query.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Tuple calculus uses {s.student_id | Students(s) ∧ s.department_id = 1}. Domain calculus for S(i,n,d) uses {<i> | ∃n ∃d (S(i,n,d) ∧ d=1)}. The former variable denotes a row; the latter variables denote separate values. Both must be range restricted.

examQuestions.question: Explain safety, range restriction and domain independence.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Safety ensures a finite answer grounded in database values. Range restriction binds variables to finite relation occurrences or appropriate constants. Domain independence means enlarging an unrelated outside universe does not alter the answer. Unrestricted complements can violate these goals.

examQuestions.question: Translate “students enrolled in every required section” into a counterexample condition. Explain an empty required set.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Return a candidate student when no required section exists for which their enrollment is absent. This becomes nested NOT EXISTS in SQL, as in the division example. If the required set is empty, every candidate student satisfies the condition. Add other eligibility conditions when the business rule needs them.
